title: Restore escape behavior and focus return for nested row actions + floating toolbars; assemble accessibility compliance kit
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Several dense table patterns (compact rows with nested row-actions that open floating toolbars) do not reliably restore focus when users dismiss the toolbar with Escape. On macOS VoiceOver, behavior is inconsistent across browsers; in NVDA the toolbar sometimes traps virtual cursor mode. This causes accessibility regressions for keyboard and assistive technology users and blocks VPAT readiness for the table widget family.

Goal: Define deterministic Escape-close + focus-restore semantics for row-action toolbars and nested controls across density variants, implement component-level primitives in the design system, and deliver a compact "compliance kit" (interaction logs, screen-reader recordings, keyboard test matrix, contrast token map, and a VPAT checklist) that engineering and reps can attach to customer audits.
acceptance_criteria: Escape closes the floating toolbar and returns focus to the original action button (or last focused cell) in 100% of tested browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) on macOS and Windows
Tab/Shift+Tab order from a closed toolbar resumes where it left off (no focus loss or focus jump outside the table)
Screen reader scenarios documented: VoiceOver macOS, VoiceOver iOS, NVDA latest, JAWS latest; each has at least one recorded example showing correct behavior
Design tokens used for toolbar focus/outline and text must meet contrast ratios: 4.5:1 for body text; 3:1 for non-text UI components per our policy (token mapping list included)
A VPAT-style checklist and a one-page compliance summary (PDF) included in the Compliance Kit linking to recordings, test matrix, screenshots, and PR references
Unit and e2e tests added: keyboard unit tests for focus restoration; Playwright scenarios simulating Escape, Tab flows, and screen-reader mode toggles
steps: Audit: generate list of table variants that use floating row toolbars (compact, regular, virtualized) and capture failing scenarios
Design: propose component API (Toolbar: onDismiss(reason), focusReturnTarget prop) and default focus-restoration behavior in tokens/spec
Implementation: collaborate with eng to add focus-manager primitive in component library and a small runtime guard to avoid focus traps in virtualized rows
Testing: record screen reader sessions, run cross-browser manual keyboard matrix, and add automated Playwright tests
Compliance package: assemble recordings, token contrast map, keyboard test matrix, PR links, and a one-page summary for customer requests
design_notes: Prefer explicit focusReturnTarget instead of implicit heuristics; implicit approaches failed in virtualized contexts when rows re-rendered on close
Use aria-expanded on action buttons and aria-controls pointing to the toolbar region for better AT mapping
Add data attribute data-focus-source on the trigger so the focus-manager can find the DOM anchor after unmounting/re-render
Avoid relying on tabindex=-1 on table cells for focus restore; instead focus the trigger or closest interactive descendant
Trade-off: forcing focus to action button may briefly move cursor for screen reader users — captured in recordings for stakeholder review
